deposits.notes: Found through the first author's public OSF projects, not cited by the screened February 2026 paper. Project title: Personality pairing improves human-AI collaboration; created and deposited 10 August 2026. Web page, node metadata, OSF Storage listing, children listing, and archive download https://osf.io/download/cyh46/ all returned HTTP 200; one stored archive and zero child nodes. ZIP SHA-256 reported by OSF: 75c2928eca3781c2c99ff5eb6f62f1237f49436ed4cf56db63eb040f80447576. The 1,018,144-byte archive was read in memory; no downloaded file was saved. Linkage to c392/S1 is supported by the same authors, same preregistrations jfzha and 95dhu (related paper arXiv:2511.13979v4, p. 14), identical recruitment dates 15-18 October 2024 and task (p. 5), and matching participant arms and total. The related paper's p. 23 explicitly identifies this data deposit and its GitHub analysis code. hh_benchmark.csv has 2,234 unique participant_id values, with treatment counts human-ai=1,258 and human-human=976. rows_checked and columns_checked refer to this participant-level file. Both submission_count and ad_quality_index have 36 blank values in human-ai and 153 in human-human; observed counts are 1,222 and 823, respectively. Observed submission counts sum to 7,266 and 3,758 (11,024 combined), but the archive does not establish that all blanks should be recoded to zero for the original paper. The associated replication code drops missing benchmark outcomes. participants.csv contains all 1,258 human-ai IDs. All creator IDs in detailed submissions, ratings, and field files join to human-ai participants; detailed human-human outputs and ratings are absent. ad_ratings.csv contains 30,126 ratings, 7,266 unique ads, 1,222 creators, and 1,168 raters; text, image and click are numeric scores, not creative text. submissions.csv has 7,537 unique ads for 1,222 human-ai creators, a different coverage from the rated corpus; do not equate these counts. field_x.csv has 1,152 ads and 651 creators, with 84 missing cpc values. field_docsend.csv has 2,760 rows for 974 ads and 619 creators; repeated ad IDs permit inspection of that human-ai subset, but the file alone does not establish the unit or totals of all 4,997 rows in c392. The README says keys share a consistent sequential-integer mapping; files normally contain the human-ai estimation sample, with hh_benchmark.csv and randomization_balance.csv covering both arms. It explicitly withholds message text, ad copy, and image URLs. There are no output-diversity scores/embeddings, ad-copy completion scores, detailed AI quality ratings, randomization/exclusion logs, or human-human team-to-output mapping. chat_labels.csv contains session IDs and numeric behavior labels for the human-ai subset, not raw chats. No license is supplied in node metadata or the README. n_files counts the one repository archive; its eleven internal files are: personality-pairing-osf/chat_labels.csv (7780062 uncompressed bytes); personality-pairing-osf/field_docsend.csv (147376 uncompressed bytes); personality-pairing-osf/process_metrics.csv (46509 uncompressed bytes); personality-pairing-osf/participants.csv (196729 uncompressed bytes); personality-pairing-osf/ad_ratings.csv (755056 uncompressed bytes); personality-pairing-osf/manipulation_markers.csv (495897 uncompressed bytes); personality-pairing-osf/submissions.csv (67921 uncompressed bytes); personality-pairing-osf/hh_benchmark.csv (384675 uncompressed bytes); personality-pairing-osf/README.md (1726 uncompressed bytes); personality-pairing-osf/field_x.csv (102094 uncompressed bytes); personality-pairing-osf/randomization_balance.csv (43183 uncompressed bytes). Public preregistration: AI Agents in Collaborative Workspaces: Effects on Creative Task Performance and Teamwork Quality; registered 14 October 2024. The paper links it on p. 11, footnote 1. The landing page returns a JavaScript shell (HTTP 200). /v2/nodes/jfzha/ and its children endpoint return 404 because this ID is a registration, not an ordinary node; the supplied node-files endpoint returns HTTP 200 with zero files. Correct endpoints /v2/registrations/jfzha/, /files/osfstorage/, /children/, and /resources/ all return HTTP 200. Registration metadata is public; zero files, zero children, zero linked resources; has_data and has_analytic_code are false. The registration describes planned conditions and measures but supplies no participant rows. License verified via https://api.osf.io/v2/licenses/563c1cf88c5e4a3877f9e96a/. The registered_from relationship points to private project 93e8m.

Public preregistration: Collaborating with AI Agents: Field Evaluations of Ad Performance; registered 15 January 2025. Linked in the paper on p. 11, footnote 1, and p. 18, Section 3.9. The landing page returns a JavaScript shell (HTTP 200). /v2/nodes/95dhu/ and its children endpoint return 404 because this ID is a registration; the supplied node-files endpoint returns HTTP 200 with zero files. Correct endpoints /v2/registrations/95dhu/, /files/osfstorage/, /children/, and /resources/ all return HTTP 200. Zero files, zero children, zero linked resources; metadata has_data and has_analytic_code are false. Contains the preregistration narrative, not observed outcome rows. License verified via https://api.osf.io/v2/licenses/563c1cf88c5e4a3877f9e96a/. Registered from the same private project 93e8m.

Also specified in the form's data_and_code.code_url. PDF p. 17, footnote 3 embeds this URL behind GitHub. HTTP 200 after redirect to https://github.com/harangju/pairit-survey. The specified recursive GitHub tree API returned HTTP 200, truncated=false; commit d901339431c7c1bb2902cfaebd66524612e0e74c has 18 files. This is survey application code plus a sampling schedule. public/submission_mockup_samples.json was downloaded and parsed in memory (HTTP 200; 1,500,391 bytes). It contains 1,300 scheduling records with session_index and samples; each samples list contains 40 ad IDs, giving 52,000 entries and 11,138 distinct ad IDs. These are planned rater sample allocations, not 1,300 observed participants or retained raters. No original creator IDs, treatment assignments, observed scores, ad copy, or images are present. pages/survey.py, lib/data.py, lib/db.py, lib/variables.py and lib/env.py were read via raw GitHub URLs (all HTTP 200); ratings are uploaded to a separate database, not distributed in this repository. The image URL template points to the now-missing mit-mindmeld S3 bucket; see the separate dead-link entry. No LICENSE file or license statement was found.

Discovered through the registered_from relationships in both paper-linked OSF preregistrations and corroborated by DataCite metadata. The public website returns only the generic OSF JavaScript shell (HTTP 200); https://api.osf.io/v2/nodes/93e8m/, /files/osfstorage/, and /children/ each return HTTP 401, with Authentication credentials were not provided. Private project; an account alone may not confer permission. File count, contents, and license cannot be confirmed. Stopped without logging in or requesting access.

Linked by the README inside the newly found OSF archive and the related paper arXiv:2511.13979v4, p. 23. Website HTTP 200; four-file root tree at commit 5031eea6ddb4aa5dc070a7e6b06c86b8bba82c23. Listed through the public repository page and each file read via raw.githubusercontent.com (HTTP 200); no additional GitHub API request used. README directs readers to https://osf.io/qr5ae and states that data omit Prolific IDs, chat text, and ad copy. replicate.py was inspected, not executed. Its hh_benchmark function (lines 708-721) calculates benchmark summaries after dropna(), including submission_count; it does not justify replacing missing benchmark counts with zero. Its detailed productivity calculation uses the 7,537-row submissions file, whereas the both-arm benchmark counts sum to 11,024 over observed rows. .gitignore excludes data/ and outputs/. Contains analysis code but no CSV data. No license file or statement found.

Indirectly found through the paper-linked GitHub survey repository: pages/survey.py constructs the ad-image URL from submission IDs in public/submission_mockup_samples.json. The first manifest ad was requested using exactly that template. HTTP 404 with S3 error NoSuchBucket: The specified bucket does not exist (mit-mindmeld). No image or ad text could be inspected; asset count, sizes, treatment/participant mapping, and content flags remain null. This is not evidence of a publicly usable text corpus.

what_we_could_compute: final.open_items[4], participant-level variance: for S1-O5, compute means, SDs, conventional independent-person SEs and observed analyzed counts by treatment using hh_benchmark.csv submission_count (1,222 human-ai and 823 human-human nonmissing observations). These are observed-case summaries. Reproducing the paper's full 2,234-person productivity statistics requires establishing how to handle 36 and 153 blank counts; do not silently treat them as zero. Human-human team-clustered precision cannot be recovered without the missing team mapping.

final.open_items[4], quality aggregation: within the human-ai arm only, ad_ratings.csv links 30,126 ratings to 7,266 ads and 1,222 creators. It allows per-ad then per-person means and person-level SDs/SEs for S1-O2, S1-O3 and S1-O4, with the aggregation rule specified. The both-arm ad_quality_index permits separate descriptive summaries, but it is a composite and cannot substitute for the three distinct c392 quality outcomes; the detailed human-human ratings are absent.

final.open_items[0] and [2], partial count checks: verify the released analyzed roster of 1,258 human-ai and 976 human-human people and count 1,168 distinct raters in the released human-ai ratings. These checks do not reconcile original allocation/attrition, human-human team totals, or the full 45,803-rating sample.

final.open_items[3], partial field checks: examine 1,152 distinct human-ai field ads (651 creators) and 2,760 DocSend rows covering 974 ads (619 creators), including repeated submission IDs and links to creators/campaigns. This permits descriptive summaries of the released human-ai subset; it cannot reconstruct the full both-arm field sample or establish the original paper's 4,997-row analysis.

Cannot compute S1-O1 diversity measures: no ad copy, embeddings or diversity scores are released. The available data also do not resolve final.open_items[1] (randomization and exclusions), [4] (human-human team/output attribution and team-adjusted precision), or [6] (ad-copy completion coding); no ad-copy completion data or detailed AI rating outcomes are included.

Read the entire 116,133-character markdown conversion, including Appendices A-L, and checked relevant PDF page text and embedded hyperlinks with PyMuPDF. The 59-page source is arXiv:2503.18238v3 (5 February 2026; title page 6 February 2026). Statement quotes are exact PDF text with line-wrap whitespace normalized. The supplied paper's p. 39 offers code/data upon request, but the later 10 August 2026 OSF deposit provides verified participant-level outcomes with both treatment arms; this is why status is public_participant_data instead of on_request. The label confirms usable participant data, not a complete release of every c392 outcome or all original analysis rows. The new deposit is from a related paper, and its scope and missing values must be respected. No original file or screening form was modified. Downloads and ZIP/CSV inspection remained in memory; repository code was not run. No login, account creation, access request, or challenge bypass was attempted. The publisher/preprint landing page https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.18238 returned HTTP 200, still lists v3 as latest, and provides PDF/HTML/TeX source but no specific ancillary data files or journal DOI.
